_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-20 10:09:52Z)**_

我找到根本原因了。先給你結論，再說怎麼修。

## 診斷結果

**`prefix + Space` 有被觸發，但選單沒渲染出來**。從 `tmux show-messages` 可以看到:
```
17:49: /dev/pts/100 key Space: display-menu -T ... -x R -y P ...
```
key binding 有正常 fire，display-menu 指令也執行了，只是**畫面沒東西**。

**根本原因**：Ubuntu 22.04 apt 裝的是 **tmux 3.2a**（2021 年版），而 macOS Homebrew 是 3.4+。你的 `keybindings.conf:242` 用了 `display-menu -x R -y P`：

- tmux 3.2a man page 明寫：
  > `R` (`-x`) = **The right side of the terminal**  
  > _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_
- 在 3.2a，`-x R` 會把選單的**左緣**對齊到終端機右邊（column 214 的 214-col 終端機），選單寬度 ~30 字元 → 延伸到 244 → 放不下 → **靜默不顯示**。
- tmux 3.3+/3.4+ 改了行為（選單會 clamp 回可視區），所以 macOS 正常。

其他線索:
- tmux 3.2a 不認得 `menu-style` / `popup-style` / `popup-border-style`（都是 3.3+ 加的）。
- `run-shell` 可執行、單獨跑 `display-menu -x R -y P ...` 回傳 exit 0，但沒實體畫面 — 完全符合「too large to fit → not displayed」。

## 修法（兩條路）

**A. 改 position，讓兩個版本都 work（推薦，低風險）**

把 `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:242` 的 `-x R -y P` 換成 `-x C -y C`（或省略，由 tmux 預設放在游標旁）。centered 會在所有版本正常顯示。

**B. 升級 Ubuntu 的 tmux 到 3.4+**

Ubuntu 22.04 apt 沒有新版，要透過 PPA / Linuxbrew / source build。你 dotfiles 的 bootstrap 會在 Linux 裝 Homebrew，但這台機器上 `brew` 沒出現在 PATH — `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/tmux` 也不存在，所以目前 tmux 是 apt 版。可考慮讓 `devtools` role 在 Ubuntu 也用 Linuxbrew 裝 tmux（類似 macOS 路徑）。

---

要我直接幫你改成 A 嗎？（一行改動，macOS 和 Ubuntu 都會正常，只是選單出現位置會從「貼右邊、由下往上長」變成「畫面正中央」。）如果你偏好維持貼右邊的視覺，B 會是更乾淨的長期方案。

---

 `./docs/tools/tmux/README.md`

```text
1	# tmux
2	
3	Managed tmux config lives under `~/.config/tmux/`, with a shim at `~/.tmux.conf` that sources the XDG entry point.
4	
5	## Source layout (in this repo)
6	
7	| Source | Deployed | Purpose |
8	|--------|----------|---------|
9	| [`dot_tmux.conf`](../../../dot_tmux.conf) | `~/.tmux.conf` | one-line shim |
10	| [`dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf) | `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` | entry point, picks theme |
11	| [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) | — | plugins + theme-agnostic options |
12	| [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) | — | all bind-keys and popup menu |
13	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | — | default theme (top status bar) |
14	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) | — | alternative theme (bottom status bar) |
15	| [`dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh`](../../../dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh) | `~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh` | responsive status bar for Catppuccin |
16	
17	This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:
18	
19	- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`
20	- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or tmux2k (bottom) — switchable at runtime
21	- Catppuccin status bar is responsive — modules adapt to terminal width (mobile-friendly)
22	- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
23	- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
24	- capture pane to clipboard helpers
25	- sesh integration for session picking
26	- `extended-keys` with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
27	- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled
28	- macOS terminal must send Option as Meta for `M-` bindings — see [ghostty.md](../ghostty.md)
29	
30	## In this folder
31	
32	- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu
33	- [themes.md](./themes.md) — Catppuccin / tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting
34	- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources
35	
36	## First-time setup
37	
38	After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.
39	
40	## Reload Config
41	
42	Most changes do not need a server restart.
43	
44	```bash
45	tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
46	```
47	
48	Or, inside tmux: `prefix + R` (shows a confirmation message after reloading).
49	
50	If a change still behaves wrong, try a new pane/window first. Only `tmux kill-server` when a terminal-capability or plugin-init issue clearly survives a reload — e.g. switching themes without leftover styling.
```
</details></tool-use>

(本機沒有安裝Linuxbrew是因爲 chezmoi.toml noRoot=true的緣故嗎？ 如果手動安裝怎麽操作？）

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-20 10:28:57Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-20 10:29:17Z)**_

是的，**`noRoot=true` 導致 bootstrap 主動跳過 Linuxbrew**。看 `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl:82-128`：

```
{{ if $noRoot -}}
# noRoot mode: Skip Linuxbrew (requires sudo for dependencies)
info "noRoot mode: Skipping Linuxbrew installation (requires sudo)"
{{ else -}}
...  sudo apt-get install -y build-essential procps curl file git
    NONINTERACTIVE=1 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL .../install.sh)"
```

原因：Homebrew 官方 installer 做兩件事需要 sudo：
1. `apt-get install -y build-essential procps curl file git`（build deps）
2. `chown` 掉 `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`（官方安裝位置，`/home/linuxbrew` 需要 root 建）

---

## 手動安裝選項（從乾淨到 hacky）

### A. 關掉 noRoot，讓 bootstrap 自己裝（推薦，如果你其實有 sudo）

```bash
chezmoi init --force  # 問 "No sudo/root access" 時選 n
chezmoi apply         # 會重跑 run_once_before bootstrap
```

### B. 請 sysadmin 跑一次官方 installer（無 sudo 帳號）

```bash
# 先請 sysadmin 確保 build deps 有裝
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential procps curl file git

# sysadmin 執行，完成後 brew 所有權會落在執行者身上
NONINTERACTIVE=1 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# sysadmin 把 /home/linuxbrew chown 給你
sudo chown -R ldw:ldw /home/linuxbrew
```
之後你就能無 sudo 用 brew（bottles 都能用，速度快）。

### C. 完全無 sudo 的 unsupported 安裝（有缺點）

Homebrew 文件列的 "untar anywhere" 方法：

```bash
mkdir -p ~/homebrew
curl -L https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/tarball/master \
  | tar xz --strip 1 -C ~/homebrew

# 加進 shell（dotfiles 的 bootstrap 已經認得 ~/.linuxbrew，
# 但 ~/homebrew 不認，你要手動 eval 或自己 symlink）
eval "$(~/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

# 或 symlink 到 bootstrap 認得的路徑
ln -s ~/homebrew ~/.linuxbrew
eval "$(~/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
```

**缺點**：Homebrew 的 prebuilt bottles 綁死在 `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`，裝在別的路徑 → 幾乎每個 formula 都要 **從 source 編譯**。tmux 編譯需要 `libevent-dev` / `libncurses-dev` 的 header，而這兩個你沒 sudo 裝不了 → 繞回原點。

---

## 針對你這台的建議

就**不要裝 Linuxbrew**。剛剛那版 ansible role 會在「noRoot + 無 brew + x86_64」這條路徑下直接抓 tmux-appimage，效果一樣（tmux 3.5a，`~/.local/bin/tmux` shim 已裝好），而且沒有 brew 那些編譯 / 路徑糾結。Linuxbrew 真正有價值的場景是你還想裝一堆其他只在 brew 有新版的工具 —— 如果只為 tmux 就太重。

如果之後你真的想跑 A（關掉 noRoot），再一起回來驗證 devtools role 的 linuxbrew 分支 priority 有沒有蓋過 appimage。

---

Linuxbrew會比apt或snap等solution好嗎？ 評估一下

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-20 10:32:09Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-20 10:32:45Z)**_

## 先說結論

**沒有絕對的「比較好」，視工具類型、情境選**。你 dotfiles 已經採取混合策略（apt + Linuxbrew + GitHub binaries + mise），這就是對的方向。下面是按維度拆解。

## 對比表

| 維度 | apt | snap | Linuxbrew | GitHub binary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 版本新鮮度 | 差（LTS 凍結） | 中～好 | **好**（近 upstream） | 好 |
| Sudo 需求 | 必要 | 必要（+ snapd daemon） | 初裝需要 | **不用** |
| 跨平台一致性 | Linux only | Linux only | **macOS/Linux 同公式** | 若 upstream 有 |
| 沙箱 | 無 | **有（AppArmor）** | 無 | 無 |
| 啟動/資源成本 | 最低 | 高（squashfs mount + 每個包帶自己 lib） | 中（bottles 有自己 lib 路徑） | 最低 |
| 系統服務 / daemon | **最佳** | 可但受沙箱限制 | 差（brew services on Linux 是 experimental） | 自己管 |
| 套件廣度 | 最大 | 中（偏 GUI） | CLI/dev 工具強 | 單點 |
| 升級控制 | 隨發行版 | 自動 refresh（不好關） | `brew upgrade` 明確 | 手動/ansible |
| 磁碟 | 省 | 肥（重複 lib + 每版本保留） | 中（~/.linuxbrew 10-15GB 常見） | 省 |
| 中斷風險 | 低（maintainer 審過） | 中（snap refresh 無預警換版） | 低（rolling but explicit） | 低 |
| 適合 noRoot | ❌ | ❌（snapd 需 systemd + sudo） | ⚠️（unsupported 模式可，但失去 bottles → 又要 dev headers） | ✅ |

## 映射到你的 dotfiles 工具分類

| 工具類型 | 推薦來源 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| **現代 CLI dev 工具**（tmux, neovim, ripgrep, fd, zoxide, starship, eza, yazi, sesh, television 等） | **Linuxbrew**（有 sudo 時）／GitHub binary（noRoot） | 版本新、跨平台 formula 名一致、可跟你的 `Brewfile.darwin` 對稱 |
| **系統 daemon / 需要 kernel / systemd 整合**（docker, openssh-server, NetworkManager, CUDA, nvidia driver） | **apt** | snap/brew 都弱，系統服務需要 root-owned unit 檔 |
| **Sandboxed GUI 或閉源軟體**（Slack, 某些 IDE, Bitwarden Desktop） | **snap** 或 flatpak 或 `.deb` | 這些來源提供自動更新 + 隔離；brew-linux 無 cask，apt 也不常有新版 |
| **語言 runtime**（node, python, ruby, rust） | **mise**（你已經在用） | 多版本切換、user-level、project-aware 比任何包管理器都強 |
| **語言的 CLI tools**（uv tools, gem, cargo install, npm -g） | **語言自帶工具** | upstream 最新、自動解決語言相依、user-level |
| **完全無 sudo 環境** | **GitHub binary + mise + uv/npm** | 這就是你 `noRoot=true` 分支做的事 |

## Linuxbrew vs apt 的關鍵取捨

**選 Linuxbrew 的情境**（如果你有 sudo）：
- 工具在 macOS + Linux 都要裝、想共用 Brewfile mental model
- 工具在 apt 版本太舊（tmux 就是典型：22.04 apt 3.2a vs brew 3.5a）
- 你已經接受 brew 在兩台機器都占 10GB+

**留在 apt 的情境**：
- 系統服務（docker engine、ssh server）
- 需要 PAM/systemd 整合（zsh 加進 /etc/shells）
- 老機器 / 磁碟吃緊 / 只想要 "works with the distro"
- 注意 security updates 會自動來

## Linuxbrew vs snap 的關鍵取捨

這兩者其實沒有正面衝突 —— **覆蓋範圍不同**：
- snap 擅長：GUI app、閉源軟體、需要沙箱保護的工具、Canonical 官方推的東西（LXD, microk8s）
- brew 擅長：CLI dev 工具、跨 macOS/Linux 一致性

若硬要二選一裝 CLI 工具：**brew 明顯勝出**（啟動快、沒沙箱路徑限制、版本新、可 pin）。snap 裝 CLI（如 snap 的 nvim、snap 的 ripgrep）常遇到讀不到 `~/.config` / `~/.ssh` 的 confinement 問題。

## 回到你的 dotfiles：我會建議的 policy

大致是你已經在做的，稍微明確化：

```
1. macOS：Homebrew 為主，Brewfile.darwin 管 GUI。
2. Linux (有 sudo)：
   2a. CLI dev 工具 → Linuxbrew 優先；apt 做為 baseline fallback
   2b. 系統服務（docker, sshd）→ apt
   2c. 需要沙箱 / 閉源 GUI → snap 或 flatpak
3. Linux (noRoot)：GitHub binaries + mise + 語言自帶工具
4. Language runtime & tools：mise、uv、cargo、gem、npm — 跨平台一致
```

你目前 role 已經走這條路，只有少數 CLI 工具（像剛剛的 tmux）因為「apt-first, 無 brew 升級路徑」而踩雷。要不要之後把這類「macOS 用 brew、Linux 也偏好 brew」的 CLI 工具整理成一個統一 block（brew 有就用 brew，沒有才 apt / appimage / GitHub binary），可以之後再做。

## 一句話總結

apt 是底，brew 補版本與跨平台，snap 補沙箱與 GUI，GitHub binary 補 noRoot —— 它們是**互補不是替代**。對你的 dev 工具，Linuxbrew 通常勝過 apt 和 snap；對系統服務相反。

# Linux Package Sources: apt vs Linuxbrew vs snap vs GitHub binaries

This repo mixes several package sources on Linux. This document explains what each is good at, the trade-offs, and the policy the ansible roles follow.

These package managers are **complementary, not substitutes**. Picking the right source for a tool is what keeps this dotfiles setup fast, portable, and safe across `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`, and `noRoot` profiles.

## Side-by-side comparison

| Dimension | apt | snap | Linuxbrew | GitHub binary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Version freshness | Poor (LTS freeze) | Medium–Good | **Good** (near-upstream) | Good |
| Sudo required | Yes | Yes (+ snapd daemon, needs systemd) | Yes at install (chown `/home/linuxbrew`) | **No** |
| Cross-platform with macOS | Linux-only | Linux-only | **Same formula names as macOS Homebrew** | If upstream ships binaries |
| Sandboxing | None | **AppArmor + strict interfaces** | None | None |
| Startup / resource cost | Lowest | High (squashfs mount + bundled libs per snap) | Medium (bottles ship own lib paths) | Lowest |
| System services / daemons | **Best** | OK but constrained by confinement | Poor (`brew services` on Linux is experimental) | Manual |
| Catalog breadth | Largest | Medium (GUI-heavy) | Strong for CLI / dev tools | One tool per source |
| Upgrade control | Ships with distro upgrades | Auto-refresh (hard to disable cleanly) | Explicit `brew upgrade` (rolling) | Manual / ansible-driven |
| Disk footprint | Small (shared libs) | Large (redundant libs, retains prev. revisions) | Medium (~/.linuxbrew 10–15 GB common) | Small |
| Breakage risk | Low (distro maintainers vetted) | Medium (silent refresh can change behaviour) | Low (rolling, explicit) | Low |
| Works in `noRoot` mode | ❌ | ❌ (snapd needs sudo + systemd) | ⚠️ Unsupported `~/homebrew` mode exists but loses bottles → needs `libevent-dev` etc. → circles back to sudo | ✅ |

## Pick-by-tool-type

| Tool type | Preferred source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Modern CLI dev tools (tmux, neovim, ripgrep, fd, zoxide, starship, eza, yazi, sesh, television) | **Linuxbrew** if sudo available; **GitHub binary** in `noRoot` | Freshest versions, shared formula names with macOS `Brewfile.darwin`, no confinement friction |
| System daemons / kernel or systemd-adjacent tools (Docker Engine, OpenSSH server, NetworkManager, CUDA, nvidia drivers) | **apt** | snap sandbox fights with host-integrated daemons; brew has no story for system services on Linux |
| Sandboxed or closed-source GUI (Slack, some IDEs, Bitwarden Desktop) | **snap** / flatpak / vendor `.deb` | brew-linux has no cask; apt versions lag; snap's automatic updates + confinement are a fit |
| Language runtimes (Node, Python, Ruby, Rust) | **mise** (already used) | Multi-version, project-aware, user-level — beats every OS package manager for this job |
| Language-ecosystem CLI tools (`uv tool`, `gem`, `cargo install`, `npm -g`) | **Language tool** | Latest upstream, auto-resolves ecosystem deps, installs to user prefix |
| Fully no-sudo environment | **GitHub binary + mise + language tools** | The `noRoot=true` branch of this repo |

## Linuxbrew vs apt

**Prefer Linuxbrew when:**

- The tool is also installed on macOS (shared mental model with `Brewfile.darwin`).
- The apt version is too old for the repo's config (e.g. tmux: Ubuntu 22.04 ships 3.2a, but our popup menu needs ≥ 3.3 — see [tools/tmux/README.md](tools/tmux/README.md)).
- You want explicit, rolling upgrades rather than waiting for the next distro release.

**Stay on apt when:**

- The tool is a system daemon or needs PAM / systemd / `/etc/shells` integration (e.g. `zsh`, `openssh-server`, `docker.io`).
- The machine is disk-constrained — apt shares system libs, brew ships its own stack.
- Unattended security updates matter more than version freshness.

## Linuxbrew vs snap

These cover different surfaces. If the choice is forced:

- **CLI tools → Linuxbrew.** snap-confined CLIs frequently hit issues reading `~/.config`, `~/.ssh`, `/tmp`, or other dotfiles because of AppArmor interface rules. Slow startup (squashfs mount + confinement enforce) is also noticeable for tools invoked often.
- **GUI apps → snap.** Fits the confinement model, auto-update works well for interactive apps that don't need deep filesystem access.

## Repo policy

Summarising how the ansible roles route tool installs:

\```
macOS:
  Homebrew (CLI + cask), mas for App Store, mise for language runtimes.

Linux with sudo (ubuntu_desktop, ubuntu_server):
  a) CLI dev tools      → apt baseline; Linuxbrew upgrade when available
                          (or when apt version fails our minimum)
  b) System daemons     → apt
  c) Sandboxed GUI      → snap or flatpak or vendor .deb
                          (dotfiles role does not manage these beyond what
                          Brewfile.linux and explicit snap tasks touch)
  d) Language tooling   → mise / uv / cargo / gem / npm

Linux noRoot (ubuntu_server + noRoot=true):
  GitHub release binaries → ~/.local/bin
  AppImage (extracted)    → ~/.local/share/<tool>/
  mise + language tools   → ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share
\```

### Example: tmux

A concrete case where the policy above matters:

1. apt installs tmux 3.2a on Ubuntu 22.04.
2. The config uses `display-menu -x R -y P` which 3.2a silently suppresses (per its man page: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_).
3. The devtools role runs a version check and upgrades:
   - If Linuxbrew is present → `brew install tmux` (3.5a+).
   - Else on x86_64 → downloads [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage), extracts it (no FUSE), drops a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`.
   - Else (non-x86_64 + no brew) → prints a warning; user must build from source or enable Linuxbrew.

This is the pattern to replicate whenever an apt-shipped tool is too old for what the dotfiles config relies on.

## Why not "just use Linuxbrew for everything"?

- **Disk:** 10–15 GB for `/home/linuxbrew` is non-trivial on VMs / servers.
- **System services:** brew cannot replace `systemctl`-managed packages cleanly.
- **First-boot cost:** every Linux provision pays the brew-install time even if 90% of tools came from apt faster.
- **Second-class platform:** Homebrew's own docs treat Linux as "best-effort"; Linux-only bottles sometimes lag macOS. `brew services` is experimental.
- **No sandbox benefit over apt** — both run as the user (or root) with full filesystem access.

## Why not "just use snap for everything"?

- **CLI tools suffer under confinement** — `snap install nvim` then trying to read `~/.config/nvim/init.lua` via a hardlink or external editor plugin can silently fail under AppArmor rules.
- **Refresh surprises** — snaps auto-refresh by default on a cadence you don't fully control; a CI or deploy script relying on a specific CLI version can break overnight.
- **Slow launch** — matters when a tool is invoked many times per shell session (shell prompts, completion scripts).
- **Server profile avoids snapd** — `ubuntu_server` deliberately keeps snapd out of the loop.

## Related docs

- [ansible.md](ansible.md) — how to run and customise the ansible roles
- [tools/tmux/README.md](tools/tmux/README.md) — the tmux ≥ 3.3 requirement and fallback install
- Root [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) — "Ansible vs Homebrew" section and per-tag tool breakdown
